title: Will it jump?
description:
Write `taken(condition, flags)`, which says whether a conditional jump with that condition is taken, given the four flags. `condition` is the part after the `j`: `"e"`, `"z"`, `"ne"`, `"nz"`, `"l"`, `"le"`, `"g"`, `"ge"`, `"b"`, `"be"`, `"a"`, `"ae"`, `"s"`, `"ns"`.

Use the flag rules from the lesson's table. For an unknown condition, return `std::nullopt`.

```
flags after cmp 3, 5:  ZF 0, SF 1, CF 1, OF 0
taken("l", ...)  = true     (3 < 5 as signed)
taken("b", ...)  = true     (3 < 5 as unsigned)
taken("g", ...)  = false
```
hints: `std::optional<T>` (from `<optional>`) holds either a `T` or nothing. `return value;` gives back a filled one and `return std::nullopt;` an empty one. A caller tests it with `if (result)` (or `result.has_value()`) and reads the value inside with `*result`.
Write one line per condition, translating the table: for example "less (signed)" is `sf != of` and "below (unsigned)" is `cf`.
The "or equal" and "greater/above" conditions combine ZF with the less-than test: `le` is `zf || sf != of`, `a` is `!cf && !zf`.
